summary: Delayed chat kickoff and intermittent timeouts after serving runtime swap and model upgrade
description: Issue summary: After the 2026-03-11 serving runtime kernel swap (auto-rollback enabled) and the redwood-2.0 model tier upgrade pushed to dedicated pools, BrightDocs began seeing delayed chat kickoff and occasional request timeouts on long-form chat completions. Impact: Customer reports elevated initial response latency (chat kickoff delay) for ~20% of requests and intermittent 504s for requests with >800 token output in us-east; user-facing sessions stall for 3–12s before stream starts. Timeline: 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC - rollout started (auto canary to 20% traffic). 2026-03-11 04:30 UTC - BrightDocs traffic routed to upgraded pools. 2026-03-12 09:15 UTC - BrightDocs support escalated to Redwood. Environment: Dedicated GPU pool (dedicated-001), prod | us-east. Steps to reproduce: 1) Call /v1/chat/completions with model redwood-2.0-small, system + user prompts totaling ~200 tokens, max_tokens 1200, streaming=true. 2) Observe that many sessions show no bytes for 3–10s, then token stream begins normally. 3) Reproduce at ~50 RPS. Expected behavior: stream starts within 100–300ms and first token emitted before 500ms under dedicated pool SLO. Observed behavior: initial bytes delayed for 3–12s in a subset of requests; some requests end with 504 gateway timeouts during initial stall. Additional notes: BrightDocs runs heavy prefix priming (few-shot templates) and long output budgets which may expose KV cache or kernel selection regressions. Customer provided sample request IDs and traces below.

investigation_notes: 03-12 10:00 - Confirmed BrightDocs on dedicated-001 pool saw TTFB regression coincident with runtime kernel swap to v1.9 candidate (canary->20%).

03-12 11:10 - Reproduced locally using customer's exact prompt envelope at 30 RPS; observed intermittent 2–8s stall before first bytes when using redwood-2.0-small with new kernel; pinning kernel to previous binary removed stalls.

03-12 13:40 - Hypothesis A: kernel selection path for small sequence lengths chooses a slower execution kernel for certain quantized weights, causing synchronous memory compaction before decode start.
03-12 14:05 - Hypothesis B: prefix/KV cache warmup combined with new batching heuristics triggers cache misses and blocks initial decode on rehydration path.

03-12 15:30 - SRE ran targeted synthetic traffic routed to candidate nodes; logs show increased mutex contention in kv_cache manager during priming phase (see github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/commit/4a2d9c).
03-13 09:00 - Noted that eu-west had far fewer occurrences, suggesting a pool-specific configuration difference (autoscaler and kernel config drift).
03-13 11:20 - Reproduced 504s when max_tokens > 800 combined with streaming=true in presence of transient KV cache miss and retry backoff policy at gateway layer.
comments: Support (Aisha): Initial handoff to SRE and product; asked for queue/tracing links and sample request IDs — provided in description.
SRE (Liam): Running focused experiment: pin kernel on a subset of nodes and monitor TTFB — started 2026-03-12 12:00 UTC.
Customer (BrightDocs - Samuel Lee): Observed session impact on user-facing editor; ~18% sessions had visible stall; willing to accept temporary routing changes.
SRE (Liam): Identified mutex contention in kv_cache during priming; working on a hotfix to avoid blocking allocate path. Will validate with canary tomorrow morning.
Support (Aisha): Communicated temporary mitigation (pin model to redwood-1.9-compat) to BrightDocs and updated ticket with mitigation steps.
Customer (Samuel): Applied pin and confirmed kickoff delay reduced to <300ms on 95% of requests; reported one remaining 504 in long-run test.
resolution_notes: Workaround implemented: 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC traffic for BrightDocs routed to fallback nodes pinned to previous kernel binary and model variant redwood-1.9-compat. Customer verified reduction in kickoff stalls. SRE implemented temporary gateway timeout extension for streaming handshakes to reduce 504s while hotfix is developed. Next steps: (1) ship kv_cache non-blocking allocate patch in serving-runtime (PR referenced), (2) run expanded canary across dedicated pools, (3) update rollout playbook to include kernel-to-model compatibility matrix. Postmortem and permanent fix ETA: 2026-03-18.
